evidence.text: Q3 fuel very likely ran well above the guide's ~$3.20/gal all-in assumption. Delta, guiding off the same mid-July curve, assumed $3.15 and realised $3.61 (+$0.46, >$500M over its July guide, and that is net of a 13c refinery benefit Aeromexico does not have). Gulf Coast jet hit $4.705 in mid-September and $4.40 on Sep-29. At ~117.5M gallons a quarter (444.7M litres in Q2), each +$0.10/gal is about $12M, roughly 0.75 points of Q3 operating margin. A $0.5-0.6 overrun is $60-75M gross, or $15-20M net after the 75% recapture Aeromexico achieved in Q2. That points to operating margin at or below the 14% low end, against a revenue line likely above the $1.62bn top end.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The sweep says the baseline history is traffic 6-Ks, not prints. Confirmed prints: Q2 2026 (2026-07-13 amc), where fuel expense came in $30M above guide and the result was called 'in line', moved +2.29% next session per the baseline row. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026) moved about +9% per StockTitan. Delta's Q3 miss on the same fuel cause sold about -3% on 2026-10-09, and AERO fell 1.33% that day in sympathy.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Aeromexico itself said fuel was 'higher than anticipated' (August traffic release, 2026-09-03) and 'a more challenging cost environment than anticipated' (September traffic release, 2026-10-06), but never quantified it or changed the guide. If the size were fully priced, the stock would have fallen through the September fuel spike. Instead it is +1.25% over 20 days, and the 'Strong Buy'/$28-46 targets and $0.24-0.61 EPS estimates are stale from before August.
evidence.independence: Company pre-warning in its own traffic release: https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results (2026-10-06). Gulf Coast spot: https://www.globalair.com/articles/aviation-fuel-spotlight-oil-is-flowing-but-jet-a-didnt-get-the-memo?id=12728. Q3 assumption and gallons: the 6-K Ex.99.1 of 2026-07-13. Shares Delta's evidence with the guidance finding below; the Q3 quarter and the Q4 guide are separate lines.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide assumed ~$3.00/gal all-in and MXN 17.6. Delta now guides Q4 at ~$4.25/gal, and USD/MXN is ~18.3-18.4 in mid-October. On ~120M Q4 gallons the fuel gap alone is ~$120-150M, about 7-9 points of the 15.5-18.5% Q4 operating-margin guide before recapture, or roughly 2-3 points net at a 75% recapture. A reset of the Q4 and FY (11-13% op margin) outlook, or a withdrawal, is very likely on the 10-20 call. Delta cut FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60 on the same cause.

If the market had priced a 2-3 point net cut to Q4 margin plus FX, AERO would have traded down with Delta's guide cut beyond its -1.3% sympathy move and would not be +1.25% over 20 days. Partly offset: the stock is already 29.5% below its high, and the CEO flagged fuel twice, so some de-rating has happened.

evidence.text: Demand and capacity sit inside or above the Q3 guide. Q3 ASMs by month were July -1.5%, August +2.3% and September +3.4%, about +1.3% for the quarter against the +0.5-1.5% guide. September international RPMs grew +6.6% on +6.3% capacity, and management called forward bookings 'healthy'. Together with US airfares up 23% y/y and Delta's +14% yield, this supports revenue at or above the $1.62bn top end through fuel recapture.
